messages.content: Write a monthly engineering update for a team of twelve, covering a migration, two hires, and a slipped deadline. Around 200 words.

Team Update — August 2026

We finished the database migration this month. All services now run on the new cluster, with no data loss and about two hours of planned downtime during the cutover window. Query latency on the main dashboard dropped by roughly 30%, which we didn't expect but will take.

Two new engineers joined the team: Priya on the platform side and Marcus on frontend. Both are ramping up on the codebase now, and pairing sessions are open to anyone who wants to sit in.

The mobile release slipped from August 28 to mid-September. The migration ate more engineering time than planned, and we chose to protect data integrity over the date. Nobody wants a rushed cutover. We'll share a firmer date once QA finishes its pass on the new build.

A few other notes: the CI pipeline is faster after last week's caching changes, and we're still hunting an intermittent flake in the payments test suite — if you've seen it, drop a note in the channel.

Thanks for the patience through the migration. It was a bigger lift than the estimate suggested, and the team handled it well. Questions or concerns about the new timeline, come find me directly.
The deadline slipped again. Update it and explain why.

The mobile release has slipped again, this time from mid-September to early October. QA's pass on the post-migration build turned up two auth-related regressions we didn't catch in staging, and we're not shipping until those are fixed and retested. The first slip cost us engineering time; this one costs us a testing pass we didn't budget for. We're tightening the QA cycle so the next date holds.

Thanks for the patience through two slips in a row. The team is doing the right thing by not rushing a build with known auth bugs. Questions or concerns about the timeline, come find me directly.
